newsitem.title: Albania: Albania ablaze as fiery protests fan out.
newsitem.headline: Albania ablaze as fiery protests fan out.

text.p: Angry Albanians, blaming the right-wing government for life savings lost in shaky pyramid investment schemes, set buildings ablaze on Sunday in the south of the poor Balkan nation and fought riot police in Tirana.

The headquarters of the state-owned oil company Albpetrol was engulfed in flames in the southern town of Patos, a company official speaking from the neighbouring town of Fier, 115 km (80 miles) south of Tirana, told Reuters.

Violence also erupted in Vlore, 150 km (100 miles) south of the capital, when protesters forced their way past an army unit and set fire to the town hall. Eyewitnesses said they heard explosions but there was no independent confirmaton.

In Tirana, riot police dispersed a 30,000-strong crowd that had gathered in central Skanderbeg Square, scene of numerous anti-government demonstrations this month, to demand that the ruling right-wing Democratic Party resign from power.
"There were injuries to many police and protesters. People were hurling stones and shop windows were smashed," an eyewitness said.
Police and plainclothes officers fired into the air to frighten the crowd and a helicopter circled overhead, the witnesses said.
Up to 2,000 demonstrators, who had joined a mass opposition rally in a Tirana soccer stadium, broke away after the meeting ended and they too ran into a wall of riot police.

State television reported more protests across southern Albania in Fier, Korce, Fushe Kruje and Lushnje, where an angry crowd on Saturday set upon Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu, who is also Democratic Party chairman.
Eyewitnesses reported a heightened military presence in Berat, scene of another violent protest on Saturday.

The disturbances, which began nearly two weeks ago, have gathered momentum across Europe's most impoverished nation, as desperate people have seen their life savings evaporate with the collapse of the once popular pyramid investment schemes.
Many Albanians blame the government of President Sali Berisha for failing to regulate the funds which lured thousands of investors with promises of high returns for a small outlay.
Opposition leaders denounced the government on Sunday and accused it of exploiting the schemes for its own gain.
"It is not the pyramid schemes which have gone bankrupt but Berisha's pyramid of power," Social Democrat leader Skender Gjinushi told the crowd in Tirana soccer stadium.
In a televised address earlier on Sunday, embattled Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi promised his government would start paying back savers' deposits from February onwards.

"With the preparations made so far we may start the systematic distribution of the money from about February 5," Meksi said, adding the government already had a stockpile of 30 billion leks ($300 million) from two pyramid schemes.
But the pledge did little to quell the unrest.

"We shall overthrow the government today at all costs," one protester at the stadium said, adding there were rumours the Democratic Party used money from pyramid schemes to fund its general election campaign last summer.
